title: Modification of a commercial DNA extraction kit for safe and rapid recovery of DNA and RNA simultaneously from soil, without the use of harmful solvents
author: Tournier, Amenc, et al.

steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free environment
steps.instruction: Treat all solutions and glassware with diethyl pyrocarbonate (DEPC) and use only certified RNase‑ and DNase‑free plastic tubes; perform every centrifugation at 4 °C and keep tubes on ice while waiting for the next step.

steps.title: Soil sample preparation
steps.instruction: Add 250 mg of soil to a Lysing Matrix E tube and freeze overnight at –80 °C (the kit originally recommends 500 mg; 250 mg is used to keep DNA below the kit’s saturation limit while allowing RNA recovery).

steps.title: Cell lysis mixture addition
steps.instruction: Add 978 µL sodium phosphate buffer and 122 µL MT buffer to the frozen soil tube; for andosol samples also add 20 mg casein to saturate high‑adsorption clays.

steps.title: Mechanical grinding
steps.instruction: Homogenize in the FastPrep™ instrument for 40 s at speed setting 6.0, place the tube on ice for 5 min, then repeat a second grinding step under the same conditions (40 s, speed 6.0).

steps.title: Initial centrifugation and supernatant transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; transfer the supernatant to a clean 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Protein precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL Protein Precipitation Solution (PPS) to the supernatant, mix by shaking the tube by hand 10 times, and keep the tube on ice while processing other samples.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and supernatant transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C to pellet precipitate; transfer the supernatant to a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: DNA binding to matrix
steps.instruction: Resuspend the Binding Matrix suspension, add 1.0 mL to the supernatant in the 2 mL tube, and place on a rotary shaker for 12 min at 23 rpm at room temperature (instead of the manufacturer’s 5 min) to ensure DNA does not contaminate the RNA‑containing wash.

steps.title: Separate DNA and RNA fractions
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 2 min at 4 °C; pellet the DNA‑binding matrix, remove the supernatant and transfer it to a clean 15 mL tube for downstream RNA purification. Keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: DNA purification – binding matrix resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA Binding Matrix in 500 µL guanidine thiocyanate (5.5 M) and transfer the suspension to a SPIN™ Filter column; centrifuge at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min. Transfer the eluate to the RNA 15 mL tube.

steps.title: DNA purification – add SEWS‑M
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL prepared SEWS‑M (ethanol added) to the filter column and gently resuspend the pellet using the force of the liquid from the pipet tip.

steps.title: DNA purification – centrifuge wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: DNA purification – dry matrix
steps.instruction: Without adding any liquid, centrifuge a second time at 14 000 × g for 2 min to dry the matrix of residual wash solution; discard the catch tube and replace with a clean one.

steps.title: DNA purification – air dry
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the SPIN™ Filter for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: DNA purification – elution
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the Binding Matrix (above the SPIN filter) in 150 µL DNase/pyrogen‑free water (DES) and incubate at 55 °C for 12 min (elution volume increased from 100 µL to 150 µL).

steps.title: DNA final centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 1 min to collect the eluted DNA in a clean catch tube; discard the SPIN filter. DNA is now ready for downstream applications.

steps.title: RNA purification – isopropanol precipitation
steps.instruction: To the supernatant obtained in step 8 (usually 2.5 mL), add 1 volume isopropanol and 500 µL sodium acetate (3 M, pH 4); gently shake and incubate for 90 min at –20 °C.

steps.title: RNA purification – ethanol wash and dry
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 30 min; wash the pellet with 70 % ethanol, centrifuge again at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min; remove ethanol and air‑dry the pellet for 5 min.

steps.title: RNA purification – resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 100 µL RNase‑free water and keep on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: RNA purification – add salt solution
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL salt solution (RNaid kit, MP Biomedicals) and transfer the mixture into a new 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: RNA purification – bind to matrix
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL RNA Binding Matrix, gently shake for 15 min at ambient temperature.

steps.title: RNA purification – wash and elute
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min; discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL RNA wash solution; centrifuge again at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min and remove supernatant.

steps.title: RNA purification – final elution and storage
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 60 µL RNase‑free water, gently shake and incubate at 55 °C for 15 min (elution volume increased from 20 µL to 60 µL). Transfer the supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL RNase‑free tube and store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Quantify nucleic acids and assess RNA integrity
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA with Quant‑iT™ PicoGreen and RNA with Quant‑iT™ RiboGreen kits according to the manufacturers’ instructions; verify RNA purity and integrity by electrophoresis on a 1 % agarose gel.

description: We adapted a commercial DNA extraction kit (FastDNA SPIN™ kit for soil, MP Biomedical, Santa Anna, CA), to recover DNA and RNA simultaneously, avoiding the use of hazardous solvents. This DNA kit, based on an SDS extraction buffer, has already shown its efficiency [1], [2]. RNA recovery was allowed because special cares were taken to work under RNase-free conditions. All solutions and glassware were treated with diethyl pyrocarbonate (DEPC) to ensure that they were RNase free and only certified RNase- and DNase-free plastic tubes were used. Each centrifugation step was performed at 4 °C and tubes were placed on ice while waiting for the next step of the procedure. RNA could therefore be purified from the DNA washing solution at the step 8 of the protocol as shown on the flow chart presented in Fig. 1 and as further described. Modifications we brought to the initial protocol of the manufacturer are detailed in italic character.1.Soil sample preparation: add 250 mg of soil sample (characteristics of soils used in this study are shown in Table 1) to a Lysing Matrix E tube and freeze overnight at −80 °C. Initially the manufacturer preconized to use 500 mg of soil. We have tested 125, 250, 500 and 750 mg, and observed that 500 mg of soil samples led already to the maximum of DNA recovered, as 750 mg of soil did not improve the yield (Fig. 2). Therefore even if 500 mg of soil increased the RNA yield by a factor of almost 4, the soil samples being processed seemed to be limited to 250 mg to keep the extracted DNA below the saturation limit of the kit and to be able to follow variations of both molecules. Of course 500 mg has to be chosen if the objective is only to maximize the quantity of DNA and RNA recovered and not to relate their recovery yield to molecular biomass estimation.2.Cells lysing: add 978 μL sodium phosphate buffer, 122 μL of MT buffer.
